Variant coverage includes SINGLE and DOUBLE store variants across direct and mmap implementations where factories expose them.
Hot-path allocation coverage confirms StoreVisitor traversal and optional prefix-filtered traversal avoid Consumer boxing and per-record allocation through qa/smoke.sh allocation gate.
Configured QA gate coverage includes ./gradlew test, ./qa/smoke.sh, and ./qa/regression.sh before final human merge handoff.
assumptions: The public range API is owned by the store module and should be exposed consistently across direct and mmap-backed SINGLE and DOUBLE store variants where those variants exist.
Tests may be authored under tests/ and fixtures under qa/fixtures/ as QA-owned surfaces; implementers must not edit tests or fixtures.
Range bounds are inclusive. Empty results are valid when no stored key falls inside the requested range.

Descending reverse scan semantics are exposed through descendingRange; ascendingRange and forEach with fromKey greater than toKey return an empty range unless the finalized design contract specifies otherwise.
Allocation gating is exercised by qa/smoke.sh and any existing allocation benchmark gate it invokes.
Optional prefix filtering must remain a primitive or precomputed scan predicate, not a secondary index or sorted-by-value query.

acceptance_tests: Empty inclusive range visits zero records for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores.
Single-key inclusive range visits exactly the requested present key for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores.
Full-keyspace inclusive range visits all populated keys in ascending order.
descendingRange visits populated keys in descending key order.
Optional prefix-filtered traversal excludes nonmatching keys without visitor hot-path allocation.
Direct and mmap implementations expose identical range semantics where both backends expose the store variant.
qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, and ./gradlew test pass before final PR handoff.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Range scans must respect the existing SINGLE and DOUBLE slot/seqlock read-stability protocol for each visited key, must not weaken publication visibility or reader/writer safety, must not mutate store state, and must not retain unstable buffer slices beyond the visitor callback.
forbidden_alternatives: Materializing range results into lists, arrays, streams, iterators, or snapshots on the hot path.
Adding snapshot, CRC, journal, checkpoint, stale-state recovery, or durability acceptance work for this non-lifecycle feature.
Allocating per visited record, boxing primitive keys, or adapting through Consumer on the visitor hot path.
hard_constraints: Visitor hot path must be zero allocation and avoid Consumer, Stream, Iterator, lambda-capturing adapters, boxed keys, and temporary collections.
Inclusive bounds must cover empty range, single-key range, full-keyspace ascending scan, and descending reverse scan.
SINGLE and DOUBLE variants must both be covered across direct and mmap-backed implementations where both variants exist.
Optional key-prefix filtering must be primitive or precomputed and must not allocate during visited entries.
Reuse existing preallocated-pool conventions from com.ull.lvc.pool where reusable helper state is required.
qa/smoke.sh must pass and the allocation gate must stay green.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: store/src/main owns API and backend implementation for SINGLE and DOUBLE direct/mmap stores; tests/ and qa/fixtures/ own pre-implementation failing coverage and fixtures; docs/Stores.md owns usage and bounds documentation; qa/ and benchmarks/ are verification surfaces only; guaranteed store and journal durability classes remain untouched.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Direct and mmap stores must share identical range semantics. Mmap scans read existing mapped slot state only and must not add snapshot, journal, CRC, checkpoint, or recovery behavior for this non-durability feature.
design_contract.public_api: Add a zero-allocation StoreVisitor interface under com.joshorig.ull.lvc.store and expose inclusive forEach(fromKey, toKey, visitor), ascendingRange(fromKey, toKey, visitor), and descendingRange(fromKey, toKey, visitor) for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores. Visitor callbacks receive primitive key metadata and stable buffer slice parameters without Consumer, Iterable, Stream, boxed keys, or per-entry allocation. Add an allocation-free optional prefix-filter overload only if existing key mapping supports it without boxing.

consolidated.problem_statement: Implement zero-allocation inclusive range-query APIs for SINGLE and DOUBLE LVC stores, including ascending, descending, and optional prefix-filtered scans without Consumer boxing or visitor hot-path allocation.
risk_register: Existing public API shape may be split between core LvcStore and store-specific facades; design must avoid incompatible or ambiguous method placement.
Naive range iteration may allocate wrappers, iterators, streams, boxed keys, or slices per record.
DOUBLE store read stability may require careful seqlock retry handling during scans to avoid observing mixed slot state.
Mmap and direct implementations may diverge if range logic is duplicated without shared semantics.
Reverse scan semantics may be confused with fromKey greater than toKey handling on ascending APIs.
Optional prefix filtering can accidentally become a secondary-index-like feature; keep it as a scan predicate only.

assumptions: The range API belongs in the store module and should be exposed consistently through direct and mmap-backed SINGLE and DOUBLE store variants.
Keys are integer slot/key ids mapped through existing IntKeyMapper and existing fixed-slot store layout; no sorted-by-value, composite-key, or secondary-index behavior is required.

Reverse ranges are valid only through descendingRange semantics; for ascending forEach/ascendingRange, fromKey greater than toKey is an empty range unless the existing design contract decides otherwise before implementation.
Allocation verification is covered by existing qa/smoke.sh allocation gate unless the QA author adds a narrower fixture under tests/ or qa/fixtures/.

acceptance_tests: Empty inclusive range visits zero records for SINGLE and DOUBLE.
Single-key inclusive range visits exactly the requested present key for SINGLE and DOUBLE.
Full-keyspace range visits all present keys in ascending order for SINGLE and DOUBLE.
Descending range visits present keys in reverse order for SINGLE and DOUBLE.
Optional prefix-filtered range avoids Consumer boxing/allocation and returns only matching keys.
qa/smoke.sh passes and reports the allocation gate green.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Range scans must respect the existing slot/seqlock read protocol for each visited key and must not weaken reader/writer safety; visitors receive only stable readable buffer slices for records accepted by the existing read invariants.
forbidden_alternatives: Do not add snapshot, CRC, journal, checkpoint, or durability acceptance work for this non-lifecycle feature.
Do not allocate per visited record, box primitive keys, or adapt through Consumer on the visitor hot path.
hard_constraints: Visitor hot path must be zero allocation and must not use java.util.function.Consumer or boxed key/value callbacks.
Bounds are inclusive for empty, single-key, full-keyspace, and reverse scan coverage.
SINGLE and DOUBLE variants must expose equivalent range behavior for direct and mmap store factories where those variants exist.
Reuse preallocated-pool conventions from com.ull.lvc.pool where temporary reusable state is unavoidable.
qa/smoke.sh and the allocation gate must stay green.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: store/src/main owns API and implementation for SINGLE and DOUBLE direct/mmap stores; tests/ and qa/fixtures/ own feature and allocation fixtures; docs/Stores.md owns usage documentation; guaranteed store/journal durability classes remain untouched.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: For mmap stores, range scans read already-persisted slot state through existing mmap buffers and must not add journal, snapshot, checkpoint, or recovery files; lifecycle recovery work is out of scope for this feature.
design_contract.public_api: Add a zero-allocation StoreVisitor interface under com.joshorig.ull.lvc.store and expose inclusive store.forEach(fromKey, toKey, visitor), ascendingRange(fromKey, toKey, visitor), descendingRange(fromKey, toKey, visitor), plus an allocation-free optional prefix-filter overload if existing key mapping supports it without boxing.
